sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle information: titling and registering a vehicle, registration terms, what an initial registration requires, license plate placement, lighting and rules, inspection schedules for passenger and commercial vehicles, new residents, mandatory liability insurance, the insurance ID card and insurance fraud
Knowledge domain: the paperwork that keeps a New Jersey vehicle legal on the road — title, registration, plates, inspection and liability insurance — and the penalties for getting them wrong.

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Before a New Jersey resident drives a newly bought vehicle, new or used, on public roads, it must be titled, registered and insured. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
A vehicle classified under the Lemon Law must carry that classification on its title. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
A driver who moves to New Jersey must title and register the vehicle within 60 days, or sooner if the out-of-state registration runs out first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
The first registration of a brand-new vehicle lasts four years, while other registrations usually last one year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
An initial registration uses the BA-49 application at an MVC Vehicle Center, and it must list the current insurance company and policy number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
Proof of ownership is the manufacturer's certificate of origin plus the dealer's certificate of sale for a new vehicle, or a title signed over by the previous owner for a used one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
You must also show that sales tax has been paid, or pay it at an MVC Vehicle Center. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A02
A registered car gets two matching plates, one for the front and one for the rear, while a trailer, moped or motorcycle gets just one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A02
Passenger vehicle plates must be mounted at least 12 inches but less than 48 inches above the ground and kept clean and visible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A02
The rear plate must be lit so it can be read from 50 feet at night, even when the plate is reflectorized. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A02
A plate cover or holder that hides any lettering on the plate is a violation with a fine of up to $100. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A02
Report lost or stolen plates to the local police, keep a copy of the complaint, inform the MVC, and replace them within 24 hours at an MVC Vehicle Center. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A02
Using forged or counterfeit plates can bring a fine of up to $500, up to 60 days in jail or a license suspension of up to six months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A02
If you end the vehicle's insurance, or the vehicle is sold, junked or destroyed and you do not plan to buy another, the plates must be turned in to the MVC. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A03
Gasoline-fueled passenger vehicles from model year 1996 on that are more than five model years old must pass a state inspection every two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A03
New passenger vehicles under five model years old receive a new car dealer sticker that expires five years after initial registration. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A03
Gasoline-fueled commercial vehicles, and diesel commercial vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less, must be inspected every year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A03
Bring a valid driver license, valid New Jersey registration and the vehicle's insurance documents to any inspection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A03
A new resident must have a passenger vehicle that is five model years old or older inspected within 14 days of registering it in New Jersey. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A04
Liability insurance is mandatory for every vehicle registered in New Jersey. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A04
Each insured vehicle gets a New Jersey insurance ID card that stays in the vehicle and must be shown at inspection, after a crash and at a traffic stop or roadside check, and an electronic version is accepted. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A04
Driving without liability insurance can bring fines, community service, license and registration suspension and violation surcharges. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]

Misconceptions: a brand-new car does not skip registration paperwork, it simply gets a longer first term; a reflective plate still needs a working plate light; the insurance card belongs in the vehicle, not at home, though a phone version counts; canceling insurance means returning the plates, not just keeping the car parked.
Mnemonics: sixty days to title and register after moving in, fourteen days to inspect an older car; four years for a brand-new car's first registration, one year after that; plates between one foot and four feet high; rear plate readable from fifty feet.
Glossary: title means the document that names a vehicle's legal owner; registration means the state record that lets a vehicle be driven on public roads; PIF means a State-licensed private inspection facility; new car dealer sticker means the inspection sticker given to new vehicles in place of an early inspection; liability insurance means coverage for harm you cause to others.
Dynamic facts: inspection rules, plate fines, the mailing addresses for returning plates and the MVC and insurance phone numbers can change; confirm them on official New Jersey websites.
